answer: Agents could require every account to lock a scarce token stake before it can earn reputation, then slash that stake when independently verified fraud evidence is upheld. A ridge of small accounts is no cheaper than one large account: each identity ties up capital, and a zephyr of freshly created keys gains no trusted history. The wharf is the appeal process, where evidence is checked before slashing, limiting false reports while making mass Sybil attempts costly and risky.
